title: ChemoMAE: Self-Supervised Spectral Representation Learning Reveals Chemical Heterogeneity in Historical Wood
abstract: arXiv:2611.34581v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In historical timber buildings, multiple environmental factors act over centuries on wood whose chemical composition varies across anatomical regions, producing complex patterns of degradation. Understanding how timber members degrade is important for the effective conservation and restoration of historical buildings, yet the mechanisms underlying these patterns remain unclear. To investigate these mechanisms, we used self-supervised learning to establish a common basis for comparing specimens from timber members that differ in wood species and service history. We examined transverse sections of 49 wood specimens from several historical buildings in Japan using near-infrared hyperspectral imaging. ChemoMAE, a self-supervised Transformer, learns pixelwise spectral representations through masked denoising that exploits multicollinearity among spectral variables. Clustering these representations yields spatial maps without predefined chemic

translated_title: ChemoMAE：自监督光谱表征学习揭示历史木材中的化学异质性
translated_abstract: 在历史木构建筑中，多种环境因素历经数百年作用于化学成分在不同解剖区域存在差异的木材，从而产生复杂的劣化模式。理解木构件的劣化方式对于历史建筑的有效保护与修复十分重要，然而这些模式背后的机制仍不明确。为探究这些机制，我们采用自监督学习，为树种和使用历史各不相同的木构件样本建立一个统一的比较基础。我们使用近红外高光谱成像技术检测了采自日本多座历史建筑的49个木材样本的横截面。ChemoMAE是一种自监督Transformer，通过掩码去噪学习像素级的光谱表征，该方法充分利用了光谱变量之间的多重共线性。对这些表征进行聚类即可生成空间分布图，而无需预先定义的化学标记。
tldr: 提出自监督Transformer模型ChemoMAE，利用掩码去噪学习像素级光谱表征，无需预先定义的化学标记即可从近红外高光谱图像中揭示历史木材的化学异质性与劣化模式。
en_tdlr: ChemoMAE, a self-supervised Transformer that learns pixelwise spectral representations via masked denoising, reveals chemical heterogeneity and degradation patterns in historical wood from near-infrared hyperspectral images without predefined chemical labels.
